title: Bright Data Pricing: Proxies, APIs and Datasets (2026)
summary: Bright Data pricing uses different billing units for each product—proxies, APIs, browsers and datasets—so costs depend on what you use.
body_markdown:
## Hidden costs and limits with Bright Data


Take the four-step workflow below: it runs on a schedule and reads targets from a Google Sheets step. It passes LinkedIn job descriptions to a GPT-6.1 Terra step that extracts keywords, and ends with a search HTTP call.


The automation around the scraper is the one meter in that pipeline that needn't grow with the number of steps.


A platform that takes Bright Data's output through HTTP or webhook steps and charges 1 credit per flow run, however many steps the run contains, keeps that meter flat (AI steps are priced separately).


Zapier's pricing page bills per task and Make's per module, so on those a ten-step version of that workflow costs more than the four-step one. Teams at MoneyGram, Moneypenny, Alan and FundingSocieties run the per-run model in production.


Bright Data's scraping stays on Bright Data's meter.


### Bandwidth you pay for but do not use


On bandwidth-priced products you pay for everything that crosses the wire, not for the fields you keep.


Everything a job listing page loads gets billed: scripts, images, tracking calls and embedded widgets. Your keyword step only needs a few paragraphs of text.


> On bandwidth-priced products you pay for everything that crosses the wire, not for the fields you keep.


You can cut this by blocking images, fonts and analytics requests in the browser session, and by caching pages that don't change between runs.


Measure the average bytes per successful record on your own targets before you compare vendors.


### Bright Data KYC verification and restricted targets


Before you can use some products and target sites, Bright Data's terms require identity and use-case verification.


Plan for this as a schedule risk: a team that starts verification late may be unable to run on the intended targets at launch.


On some domains the pricing or handling is premium, which means the same request can cost more on one site than another. Check the docs for your specific domains before you fix a cost-per-record figure.


### Bright Data minimums, overages and expiring balances


When a plan has a monthly minimum, a variable cost becomes a fixed one. If your usage dips in a slow month, you still pay the floor, so the effective rate per gigabyte or per thousand requests rises as usage falls.


Model the floor against your lowest-volume month, not your average.


Usage above the plan can bill at a different rate, so a successful scale-up may cost more per unit than the plan you priced.


Prepaid balances can lapse, so unused credit may be lost instead of rolling forward. Read the renewal and expiry terms before you buy ahead.
